display.purpose: Page titles inside an ink band. One per page.

headline.purpose: Entity names within a band, such as two drivers on a rivalry page.

title.purpose: Card and panel headings, track and driver names in lists.

body.purpose: Prose and table cells. Cap running prose at 65 to 75ch.

label.purpose: Section eyebrows, table headers, units, season markers. Always mono, always uppercase.

shadows.name: ambient-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover only, on interactive cards. Tinted toward ink, never neutral black.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on inputs and controls.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Default duration for color, border-color, and background state changes.

components.name: Header Band

components.name: Panel
components.description: White content panel on paper. Flat at rest; border does the work.

components.css: .ds-panel { background: var(--cgr-card, #fff); border: 1px solid var(--cgr-border-card, #d9d6cd); border-radius: 5px; padding: 16px 18px; font-family: var(--cgr-font-body, sans-serif); } .ds-panel-eyebrow { font-family: var(--cgr-font-mono, monospace); font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.18em; color: var(--cgr-text-muted, #7a766b); margin-bottom: 13px; } .ds-panel-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 9px 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--cgr-border-hairline, #ece9e1); font-size: 13px; color: var(--cgr-text-body, #33312a); } .ds-panel-num { font-family: var(--cgr-font-mono, monospace); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Interactive Card
components.description: Panel that links somewhere. The only element in the system that lifts.
components.css: .ds-card-link { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; padding: 10px 12px; background: var(--cgr-card, #fff); border: 1px solid var(--cgr-border-card, #d9d6cd); border-radius: 5px; text-decoration: none; transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-card-link:hover, .ds-card-link:focus-visible { border-color: var(--cgr-border-hover, #a8a496); box-shadow: 0 10px 22px rgba(22,20,15,0.09); outline: none; } .ds-card-name { font-family: var(--cgr-font-display, sans-serif); font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; color: var(--cgr-text-primary, #16140f); } .ds-card-score { font-family: var(--cgr-font-mono, monospace); font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; color: #1c7a4a; }

components.name: Navigation
components.description: Sticky ink bar with the league's 3px racing-red signature stripe.

components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 26px; min-height: 62px; padding: 8px 26px; background: var(--cgr-ink, #16140f); border-bottom: 3px solid var(--cgr-red, #e8232c); } .ds-nav-brand { font-family: var(--cgr-font-display, sans-serif); font-weight: 700; font-size: 19px; color: var(--cgr-text-on-dark, #f7f5ef); } .ds-nav-links { display: flex; gap: 26px; } .ds-nav-link { font-family: var(--cgr-font-body, sans-serif); font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; color: var(--cgr-text-on-dark-muted, #b3afa4); text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.15s; } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: var(--cgr-text-on-dark, #f7f5ef); } .ds-nav-link-active { color: var(--cgr-text-on-dark, #f7f5ef); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cgr-red, #e8232c); padding-bottom: 3px; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: Inert badge for counts and categories.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-block; font-family: var(--cgr-font-mono, monospace); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--cgr-text-muted, #7a766b); background: var(--cgr-chip, #e3e1d8); border-radius: 3px; padding: 2px 5px; }

components.name: Signal Chip
components.description: Gold badge reserved for exceptional facts: sprint races, records, bests.

components.name: Split Bar
components.description: Two-way comparison bar. Always paired with the literal values; the bar reinforces, never encodes alone.

narrative.overview: CGR League is a printed motorsport record book rendered in a browser. Paper stock under ink headers, condensed uppercase titles, figures set in mono. Its authority comes from looking like a published annual of record, something a league would keep on a shelf, not from looking like software. The system rejects generic dark SaaS and the official F1 website by name; both treat stats as content to be decorated, and here the stats are the product. Density is a virtue: a sparse layout reads as unfinished, so pack information with precision and let hairline rules do the separating that whitespace would do elsewhere.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink duality: dark bands introduce, light panels inform
Condensed uppercase display type against wide-tracked mono labels
Flat at rest, hairline-ruled, no resting shadows
Real team liveries used as data encoding, never as decoration
Numbers set in mono and tabular everywhere they are compared

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: There is a single ink (#16140f). It is the band background and it is the body text color. Never introduce a second near-black; never reach for pure #000.

rules.name: The Red Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: Racing Red marks identity and active state, nothing else. If red appears on a surface that is neither the nav rule, the logo, an active indicator, nor a focus ring, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Livery Rule
rules.body: Team colors are data encoding, never styling. When two liveries encode two series, they must clear both a delta-E floor and a hue gap before use; substitute a contrasting partner hue when they cannot.

rules.name: The Mono Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every figure that gets compared against another figure is set in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals. A number in the body font is a number nobody is comparing.

rules.name: The Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Sections are introduced by an 11px wide-tracked uppercase mono label, never by a large heading. The heading weight belongs to the ink band; inside the paper, sections whisper.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: No surface carries a shadow at rest. Audit test: screenshot the page and squint. If you see soft gray halos under stationary elements, the system has drifted.

dos: Do build every new page on the --cgr-* tokens in frontend/src/styles/cgr-tokens.css. Page shell is --cgr-paper with --cgr-text-primary and --cgr-font-body.
Do open each page with an ink band: mono eyebrow, condensed uppercase display title.
Do set every comparable figure in --cgr-font-mono with tabular numerals.
Do separate rows with 1px #ece9e1 hairlines and let density carry credibility.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest and move border-color on hover over 0.15s.
Do validate any two-series color pair for both delta-E and hue gap before shipping it, and give every series a text label so identity is never color-alone.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on anything that animates.
donts: Don't build on the legacy :root tokens in index.css (--bg, --surface, --text-bright, --accent). A new page styled with them renders dark-on-dark against the current light surfaces.
Don't produce generic dark SaaS: no blue-accent card grids, no opacity-token chrome, no glassmorphism, no floating panels with resting shadows.
Don't imitate the official F1 website: no marketing furniture, no brand promotion competing with the data.
Don't use Racing Red as a fill, a heading color, or an accent on anything that is not identity or active state.
Don't use a team livery as decoration. Liveries are data encoding and must pass the legibility gate first.
Don't use border-left or border-right above 1px as a colored stripe on cards, rows, or callouts.
Don't pad a page out with whitespace to make it feel designed. Sparse reads as unfinished here; add information instead.
Don't put a large heading inside the paper region. Sections are introduced by mono eyebrows; the display weight belongs to the band.
